result.title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
result.summary: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association. We introduce EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. EgoActionBench contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. To evaluate such dense predictions, we propose an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall, jointly capturing what happens, when it happens, and which hand performs it. We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench and further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes. EgoAction improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points on the two backbones, and both adapted models outperform all open-source baselines. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations of current models in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association, highlighting the gap between general video understanding and the action understanding required for embodied intelligence.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EgoActionBench，将第一视角连续操作表示为带时间定位与左/右手归属的原子动作，包含 1,407 段视频和约 4.1 万条人工精修标注，并设计兼顾语义保真、时间重叠与动作精确/召回的评价协议，测试 20 个基线并对两个骨干做 SFT 加 RL 适配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其细粒度时间定位与手-动作关联标注、以及按内容一致性匹配预测的协议，可能可供核查 VLM 内部状态是否保留任务必要的局部视觉证据；但论文本身面向视频描述评测，未涉及 latent 状态或推理期机制，联系较外围。
